title: Under Pressure: Emergence of Cefiderocol Resistance in E. hormaechei Pneumonia
content: Cefiderocol is an important treatment option for New Dehli metallo-β-lactamase (NDM)-producing Enterobacterales, but resistance can emerge during therapy. We describe a patient with a history of bilateral lung transplantation who developed respiratory failure and a persistent Enterobacter hormaechei infection. E. hormaechei was initially cultured on hospital day (HD)15 from the respiratory tract. blaNDM-5 was detected and the isolate was resistant to all β-lactams tested, including ceftazidime-avibactam, but were susceptible to aminoglycosides. After 41 days of cefiderocol, subsequent E. hormaechei isolates from the lung were resistant to cefiderocol. E. hormaechei was also isolated from the patient’s bloodstream near the end of the hospitalization, and was cefiderocol susceptible. To better understand mechanisms of cefiderocol resistance, whole-genome sequencing of five available clinical isolates was completed on long-and short-read platforms. No single nucleotide variants (SNVs) or small insertions/deletions distinguished the isolates. Instead, resistant isolates uniquely harbored two IS5-family insertions: IS903B truncating a CirA-like TonB-dependent siderophore receptor by approximately 30 amino acids, and ISKpn26, immediately upstream of tolC. These findings suggest cefiderocol uptake, possibly combined with efflux upregulation, may have arisen through transposition. Aztreonam-avibactam was active in vitro against all isolates. The patient received ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam with appropriate serum aztreonam concentrations, but clinically deteriorated and died. This case shows that resistance mechanisms can be missed by SNV-focused sequencing analyses, underscores the value of long-read sequencing, and supports considering combination therapies for NDM-producing Enterobacter infections. Further functional studies are needed to confirm the roles of cirA-like and tolC insertions.
